summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and prior toe amputations was admitted due to gangrene and infection of the right fourth toe. He underwent amputation, and tissue cultures confirmed E. coli and anaerobic bacteria. He was treated with intravenous antibiotics, initially vancomycin and Zosyn, then transitioned to outpatient ertapenem via a newly placed PICC line for a six-week course. His blood pressure was elevated during admission, prompting an increase in spironolactone dose. Kidney function remained stable within his baseline, and he was discharged home in stable condition with plans for wound follow-up, infectious disease management, and weekly lab monitoring.
